rule: Use for the whole world, the earth set against the heavens, and the creation and flood texts (Gen 1 to 2, 'all the earth'). Gen 1:10 names the dry land 'Earth'.
reason: KJV: earth x711. The Hebrew word covers both the world and a territory, and English needs two words. The sense label is recorded in the draft alignment.

rule: Use for a territory, region, nation or the soil of a place (land of Canaan, people of the land). When unsure between earth and land, use land and add a verse note of kind difficulty.
reason: KJV: land x1509, country x92, countries x48, lands x34. Land is the larger sense and the safer default.

rule: A plural participle used as a noun is 'inhabitants'. Hiphil is 'cause to dwell'. The Hiphil marriage idiom gets a verse note.
reason: KJV: dwell, dwelt, inhabit(ants), abide ~ 700 of 1082 uses. BDB lists sit first, but dwell is the plain English word for residing.

rule: Use for the body posture, sitting in judgement or at a gate, and on a throne. Gen 23:10 (Ephron sitting among the sons of Heth) is decided in the translation session with a verse note.
reason: KJV: sit/sat ~ 190 uses. Keeps the physical sense visible where the context needs it.

allowed: cross; go over; go through; pass by; pass on; pass away
rule: Choose the particle from the Hebrew preposition and the context. Money 'passing' to the merchant (Gen 23:16).
reason: KJV: over x174, pass x93, through x59, by x27. One verb with particles keeps the uses linked.

rule: Use when the object is a command, covenant, word of Yahweh or law.
reason: KJV: transgress ~ 17 uses. 'Pass over a command' would read as ignoring it. 'Overstep' keeps the picture of crossing and the sense of breaking.

rule: Keep 'soul' in every use, including 'living soul' (Gen 1:20 to 2:19). Uses like 'my soul' for 'I' and the idiom in Gen 23:8 stay literal in the text and are explained in a verse note.
reason: KJV: soul x474 of 754. One word keeps all uses linked and leaves interpretation to the reader and the notes. Alternative: separate senses being, life, person. Decision needed.

rule: Shut up when the object is confined in a place (calves, a prisoner). Withhold when the object is something given (mercies, a tomb, Gen 23:6).
reason: 18 uses. KJV: shut up, restrain, withhold, refrain, stay. YLT: restrain in most places.

rule: Reserve 'mourn' for the root אָבַל, 'weep' for בָּכָה. Noun forms follow: lamentation.
reason: 32 uses. KJV: lament x13 and mourn x14. Using lament here keeps mourn free for the other root.
46 uses. KJV: meet, fall upon, reach, come upon. Basic sense is to meet or strike against.

rule: Use when the one who meets does so on behalf of another (Gen 23:8 'meet for me with Ephron'; Isa 53:12; 59:16). Check each use against the sheet.
reason: KJV: intercession x4, intreat x3. The 'for' phrase marks the sense.

rule: In the phrases על כן and לכן use 'therefore'. 'And it was so' (ויהי כן) keeps 'so'.
reason: 770 uses. KJV: so, thus, therefore. The fixed phrase 'and it was so' in Gen 1 must stay uniform.

rule: 'Prince of God' (Gen 23:6) stays literal with a verse note that God may mark the superlative.
reason: 130 uses. KJV: prince, ruler, captain, chief. ASV and YLT read 'prince of God' in 23:6; KJV reads 'mighty prince'.
